selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What problem is being addressed at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: It is dealing with being careless or lazy about worship and the required prayers because of worldly busyness.

questions.question: What answer does the passage give to the idea that a person was made only for this world?
questions.answer: It rejects that idea and teaches that life has a greater purpose than worldly survival.

questions.question: What does the passage say about many things people call worldly duties?
questions.answer: It says many of them are actually small matters that do not deserve so much attention.

questions.question: What does the passage say about many busy activities in life?
questions.answer: It says many of them are not truly necessary and are often unnecessary interference in lesser matters.

questions.question: How does the passage show that worldly busyness is often exaggerated?
questions.answer: It says many so-called duties are actually minor issues people involve themselves in too much.

questions.question: What is the danger of filling life with needless information?
questions.answer: It wastes time that should be used for more important duties and preparation.

questions.question: What example is used to show how foolish a weak excuse can be?
questions.answer: A worker is offered great treasure for only ten minutes of effort but refuses because of a tiny loss in wages.

questions.question: What does the orchard stand for in the comparison?
questions.answer: It stands for this world where a person works for provision.

questions.question: What two “mines” are discovered through prayerful and sincere work?
questions.answer: One is reward connected to what grows, and the other is charity-like reward from what others consume.

questions.question: What are the two major gains connected with prayer and work together?
questions.answer: They bring blessed worldly provision and reward for the life after death.

questions.question: What does the passage ask about the reason for being weak in worship?
questions.answer: It asks whether the reason is too much worldly work or the struggle to earn a living.

questions.question: What question is asked about worldly occupations and prayer?
questions.answer: It asks whether worldly busyness is really the reason a person becomes careless with worship.

questions.question: How does the passage use animals to make its point?
questions.answer: It says humans should not lower themselves to living only for food and survival like animals.

questions.question: What does the passage say is wrong with living only for worldly needs?
questions.answer: It lowers a human being beneath his real purpose and higher abilities.

questions.question: What does the passage say about many things people get busy with?
questions.answer: Many are side matters that people treat as important when they are not.

questions.question: Why are those examples criticized?
questions.answer: They waste valuable time on things that do not help a person in the most important duties.

questions.question: In the example, what does the small wage cut represent?
questions.answer: It represents the minor worldly cost or time spent on prayer.

questions.question: What effect do prayers have on the spirit and heart, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They refresh the spirit and give breathing room and relief to the heart.

questions.question: What does abandoning obligatory prayer do to the results of that labor?
questions.answer: It narrows the results down to weak worldly gain only.

questions.question: How does sincere intention affect ordinary labor?
questions.answer: It can turn ordinary labor into something that earns spiritual reward.

questions.question: What kind of self is being spoken to in this passage?
questions.answer: It is the self that is attached too much to worldly life.

questions.question: What wrong idea about human life is challenged here?
questions.answer: The wrong idea is that people exist only to work for worldly needs.

questions.question: How is daily work in this world pictured in the comparison?
questions.answer: It is pictured as labor in a garden or orchard for one’s provision.

questions.question: What attitude does the passage criticize when speaking about such information?
questions.answer: It criticizes acting as if one will stay in this world for an extremely long time.
